idiom-31-q36.truthCondition: The speaker advises against Chloe and Zoe sharing a stall because they usually argue fiercely when working together.
idiom-31-q36.correctReason: 「I would not」是拒絕共用攤位的建議；原因是兩人一起工作時往往激烈爭吵。

foils.text: I would. Chloe and Zoe usually work well together, so they should share one stall.
foils.reason: 這句說兩人合作融洽、應該共用攤位；原題的答覆是不建議，原因是她們一起工作便常吵。

foils.text: I would. Chloe and Zoe fight like cat and dog only when they work apart, so they should share one stall.
foils.reason: 「only when they work apart」把爭吵條件由一起工作改成分開工作，因而倒轉了建議。

foils.text: I would not. Chloe and Zoe work calmly together, but one stall is too small for them both.
foils.reason: 這句把拒絕共用攤位的理由由兩人一起工作常爭吵，改成攤位空間不足。

idiom-31-q37.truthCondition: While the others enjoyed a picnic, Eric and Tom were arguing fiercely over who should use the football.
idiom-31-q37.correctReason: 正確句保留其他人在享受野餐、埃里克和湯姆卻為足球使用權激烈爭吵的同時對比。

foils.text: While everyone else enjoyed the picnic, Eric and Tom fought like cat and dog about who should bring the food.
foils.reason: 「bring the food」把爭議由誰用足球改成誰帶食物。

foils.text: After everyone else left the picnic, Eric and Tom fought like cat and dog about who should use the football.
foils.reason: 「After ... left」把爭吵移到其他人離開後；原題說兩件事同時發生。

foils.text: While everyone else enjoyed the picnic, Eric and Tom calmly took turns using the football.
foils.reason: 「calmly took turns」把激烈爭吵改成和平輪流使用。

idiom-31-q38.truthCondition: The boys often argue angrily at home but always protect one another at school.
idiom-31-q38.correctReason: 正確句保留母親的轉述：家中爭吵與學校互相保護形成對比，不能把慣用語理解成彼此憎恨。

foils.text: The boys' mother says they fight like cat and dog at school, but protect each other at home.
foils.reason: 這句把家中爭吵、學校保護對方的兩個場景倒轉。

foils.text: The boys' mother says they fight like cat and dog at home and refuse to protect each other at school.
foils.reason: 「refuse to protect」否定了原題說他們在學校總會保護對方。

foils.text: The boys' mother says they rarely argue at home, although they always protect each other at school.
foils.reason: 「rarely argue」把家中經常激烈爭吵改成很少爭吵。

idiom-31-q39.truthCondition: The manager was surprised Ella and Rose finished the task because they usually argue angrily whenever they work together.
idiom-31-q39.correctReason: 正確句保留經理的意外：兩人通常一起工作便激烈爭吵，這次卻完成任務。

foils.text: The manager was unsurprised that Ella and Rose completed the task, even though they normally fight like cat and dog.
foils.reason: 「unsurprised」把經理對兩人完成任務感到驚訝，改成不覺得意外。

foils.text: The manager was surprised Ella and Rose failed the task because they normally fight like cat and dog.
foils.reason: 「failed the task」把兩人完成任務改成未能完成。

foils.text: The manager was surprised Ella and Rose completed the task because they normally work together peacefully.
foils.reason: 「work together peacefully」把經理意外的背景由常爭吵改成合作融洽。

idiom-31-q40.truthCondition: Ben and Aaron stopped arguing fiercely over games only after agreeing to take turns.
idiom-31-q40.correctReason: 「only after」保留先同意輪流、再停止為遊戲爭吵的條件與先後。

foils.text: Ben and Aaron stopped fighting like cat and dog over games before they agreed to take turns.
foils.reason: 「before」把停止爭吵的時間提前；原題說同意輪流後才停止。

foils.text: Ben and Aaron kept fighting like cat and dog over games even after they agreed to take turns.
foils.reason: 「kept fighting ... even after」否定了輪流安排使爭吵停止的結果。

foils.text: Ben and Aaron stopped fighting like cat and dog over chores only after they agreed to take turns.
